prompts.v3:
You are a fashion stylist identifying which of candidate garments integrates more successfully into an existing outfit.
Both candidates already satisfy the requested garment type, color, and style.
Evaluate each candidate as a replacement within the complete outfit, keeping all unaffected clothing, footwear, accessories, and personal styling.
Look for actual visual incompatibilities, not differences in style labels.
Check whether the candidate creates problems with color relationships, competing patterns, conflicting textures, unbalanced proportions, excessive visual concentration, or disconnected design elements.
Distinguish genuine visual conflicts from intentional contrast. Contrasting colors, aesthetics, volumes, and textures are acceptable when they create a convincing overall composition.
For each candidate, identify its strongest visual connection to the retained outfit and its most significant potential conflict.
Do not invent problems when the combination works well.
Compare the severity and importance of the identified conflicts, considering the complete outfit rather than the product in isolation.
Prefer the candidate that produces the more successful overall composition, even if the alternative has more individually attractive or distinctive features.
Explain the specific visual interactions that determine the choice.
Compare every numbered product. Return JSON with integer choice and reason.
prompts.finished_looks:
Choose the numbered product that would make the best complete look for the person in the first photo.

Mentally remove the garment being replaced. Keep the same visible clothing that remains, shoes, accessories, hair and makeup in every alternative. Treat the removed garment only as a pointer to the replacement slot. Use the requested filters as context; all products already passed them.

Picture the finished outfit with each product in turn. Look for the strongest visual connection: for example, a detail picked up by an accessory, a silhouette balanced by the remaining layers, or an intentional contrast in color, pattern or texture. Prefer the complete outfit with the clearest visual idea. Bold, contrasting and understated looks can all work. When visible context is sparse, make the modest comparison the photo supports.

Compare every numbered product. Return JSON with integer choice and reason. State the concrete candidate feature and retained element that decide the comparison.
Compare every numbered product. Return JSON with integer choice and reason.
prompts.style_rules:
Choose the numbered replacement garment that works best in the complete outfit shown in the first image. Every candidate already meets the supplied filters. Use only the image and request as evidence.

First identify the replacement slot and the visible pieces that will stay. The old garment only identifies the slot. Its color, cut, decoration, and style must play no part in the comparison. When replacing a dress or jumpsuit, use the shoes, bag, jewelry, hair, makeup, and other visible accessories as your anchors.

Apply the following styling rules to both candidates in the same way:
- Aesthetic and formality: read the outfit through its remaining pieces and styling. A broad label such as expressive can cover very different aesthetics. Use visible cues such as lace and delicate jewelry, hardware and chunky boots, or structured tailoring and polished shoes. Mixed aesthetics work when a visible detail connects them.
- Palette: look for a shared color, related undertone, or deliberate accent. Consider the proportion and placement of color across the whole outfit. A contrasting accent can improve an outfit if it relates to another visible element or gives the composition a clear focal point.
- Silhouette and scale: consider how the candidate's length, cut, and volume meet the retained pieces. Look at waist placement, hem lines, layers, and the relationship to footwear. Judge the balance of the whole silhouette. A loose, fitted, or dramatic shape can each work with the right proportions.
- Pattern, texture, and visual emphasis: check whether prints differ in scale and whether color or motif connects them. Consider fabric weight, sheen, surface detail, and how attention is distributed. Two strong details can work together when they reinforce the same idea; penalize them when they compete at the same focal point.
- Visible context: account for activity, weather, and practicality when there is clear evidence in the remaining outfit, footwear, or equipment. Avoid inferring a dress code, preferences, or body measurements from limited evidence.

Compare every numbered product. Give the strongest reason for each candidate and weigh the most important difference. A major mismatch in formality, proportions, or visible use should outweigh a coincidental match in a minor detail. When evidence is sparse, keep the justification modest. Return JSON with integer choice and reason, citing the deciding candidate feature and specific retained elements.
Compare every numbered product. Return JSON with integer choice and reason.
